_doc: Commute-to-Manhattan reference data, one entry per target town. REFERENCE, NOT SCRAPED — this is hand-curated from NJ Transit / Lakeland / Coach USA / Trans-Bridge timetables, unlike sales.csv which comes from public records. Kept in its own file so it can never be mistaken for sale data. Flattened into share/transit.csv by build_share.py.
_method: Verified 2026-07-13 against current official weekday timetables (NJT rail eff. 5/31/26 and 3/15/26; NJT bus issued 7/1/26; Lakeland, Coach USA, Trans-Bridge current schedules). Times are TOTAL AM-PEAK minutes from the town's station/stop to Manhattan (NY Penn for rail, Port Authority Bus Terminal for bus), INCLUDING transfer and wait time where a transfer is required. Unknown => null, never a guess. 2026-07-13: added the 20 towns that had no entry (incl. Westfield, Cranford, Summit, Short Hills), each verified against the same official weekday timetables. 2026-07-17: added the last 4 towns (Mountainside, Bernardsville, Mountain Lakes, East Hanover) computed from NJ TRANSIT'S OWN GTFS FEEDS (rail_data.zip / bus_data.zip) rather than read off a PDF — the feed is the timetable, so these meet the same 'verified against the official weekday timetable' bar. Method proved against rows already here before use: Short Hills recomputes to 39-47 and Summit's median to 47, both exactly matching the hand-curated values, and Westfield correctly shows no one-seat ride. AM-peak = arrival at NY Penn / PABT between 06:00 and 10:00 on an ordinary weekday (rail 2026-09-04, bus 2026-09-16 — holiday dates carry a different service_id set and were excluded). Reported minutes are the MEDIAN peak trip, with the full range in each note.
_caveats: AM peak weekday only. Off-peak, reverse-peak and weekend service differ sharply — several bus routes do not run at all on weekends.
For towns with no station, train_minutes_to_manhattan is the ride from the NEAREST station and EXCLUDES the drive/park time to reach it. Add 10-20 min.
'Rush-only' bus routes (NJT 101/102/105, Lakeland 78, Trans-Bridge) run a handful of AM trips — 'a bus exists' is not 'frequent service'. See notes.
DeCamp Bus Lines (formerly THE Essex County carrier to PABT) discontinued all commuter routes April 2023 and shut down entirely Feb 2025. Any source claiming DeCamp service is stale.

The 4 towns added 2026-07-17 are GTFS-derived and cover NJ TRANSIT ONLY. The feed has one agency ('NJ TRANSIT BUS'), so Lakeland / Coach USA / Trans-Bridge do NOT appear in it. Where such a row says has_bus_to_port_authority=false it means 'no NJT bus to PABT', never 'no bus' — Boonton's own row shows how much a private carrier can change the answer (Lakeland 46 at 55 min vs 80 by rail).

towns.notes: RVL: no peak one-seat ride, every NY time flagged 'change at Newark Penn'. Verified peak trips 50-59 min (rarv.pdf). Bus 113 from Westfield station (North Ave at Elm) to PABT a consistent 58 min, every 10-15 min at peak - frequent, not rush-only.

RVL: no peak one-seat ride, change at Newark Penn. Verified peak trips 45-53 min. Cranford gets the 'X' trains, express between New York and Cranford. Bus 113 from Cranford station 47 min, frequent AM service - the fastest option here.
Raritan Valley Line has NO one-seat ride at AM peak — every peak train is flagged 'change at Newark Penn'. Bus stop on North Ave; exact boarding times unverified.

RVL: no peak one-seat ride. AM peak runs a SKIP-STOP pattern - some peak trains serve Westfield/Cranford and skip Fanwood, others the reverse. Verified 56-64 min. Bus 113 (Midway Ave at Terrill Rd) 68 min - slower than rail.
No station of its own — the station was RENAMED from 'Scotch Plains' to 'Fanwood' in 1895 when the borough formed. RVL: no peak one-seat ride.

No station; nearest is Westfield ~2.3 mi (Summit is ~2.5 mi and has the better one-seat M&E ride, worth the extra 0.2 mi). Rail figure is Westfield's own — RVL, no peak one-seat, change at Newark Penn. THE BUS BEATS THE TRAIN HERE: NJT 114 from Mountain Ave at Roberts Ln runs 38 AM-peak trips to PABT, 45-72 min, median 54 — i.e. faster than the 55-min rail ride AND without the 2.3 mi drive to Westfield first. NJT 117 also reaches PABT (48 min) but is rush-only: 4 AM trips. Computed 2026-07-17 from the NJT bus GTFS on an ordinary Wednesday (2026-09-16); the feed IS the timetable.
No station, but Rahway is a direct 45-min ride. The 112 bus is a slow local via Elizabeth — 90 min, far worse than rail. Take the train.

No station. Millburn (~2 mi) has one-seat Midtown Direct, verified 34-43 min - excludes drive/park. NJT 70 serves Springfield but terminates in NEWARK, not PABT; Lakeland 78 and Community Coach 77 do not stop here. Bus=false is an absence-of-evidence finding after checking NJT, Lakeland and Coach USA.
No station and no in-town PABT bus. Nearest bus stops are 114/117 on Watchung Ave in North Plainfield.
A CDP inside Woodbridge Twp with no station of its own, but METROPARK is the practical station: NEC express, big park-and-ride, 40 min direct to Penn. One of the best commutes in the target set.

One-seat Midtown Direct available throughout the AM peak, verified 42-52 min. Some peak trains run to Hoboken instead. Lakeland 78 from Summit Park & Ride 35-38 min; express trips skip Summit. The best transit town on this list.

Only a SMALL number of AM-peak Gladstone trains are Midtown Direct one-seat rides (verified 6:30->7:28, 7:10->8:12); most peak Gladstone columns terminate at Hoboken and riders change at Summit. Lakeland 78 is RUSH-ONLY: just 4 AM eastbound trips, 50-60 min.

Gladstone Branch: only TWO AM one-seat 'Midtown Direct' trains (6406, 6410) — every other peak train goes to Hoboken, so the typical rider transfers at Summit. Marked direct=false as the realistic case.

Millburn station, M&E Midtown Direct — one stop INSIDE Short Hills, so faster. Published guides put peak Midtown Direct at ~35 min (range 30-45); Short Hills' own row is a timetable-verified 39-47. 38 is the consistent read. CONFIDENCE MEDIUM: sourced from commuter guides, not from a timetable I opened — unlike Short Hills. Same Hoboken-train caveat applies: not every AM-peak train is Midtown Direct.

Midtown Direct to NY Penn verified 39-47 min. CAVEAT: several AM-peak Short Hills trains (7:42, 8:03, 8:42) are HOBOKEN trains, not Midtown Direct - riders must time to the MD trains. No commuter bus to PABT (not on Lakeland 78's stop list; Community Coach does not serve Millburn Twp).

No station. Metuchen (~5 mi, NEC) is one-seat to NY Penn, verified 45-50 min - excludes a real 5-mi drive. The NEARER stations (Dunellen, Plainfield, ~3-4 mi) are Raritan Valley Line, which has NO peak one-seat ride, so the farther NEC station is the better commute. No PABT bus: South Plainfield is NOT on the NJT 114/117 stop list (issued 7/1/26) despite third-party trip planners claiming otherwise.

towns.nearest_station_if_none: Dunellen (~4 mi, RVL); also Berkeley Heights / Basking Ridge (Gladstone)
towns.notes: train_minutes is NULL on purpose: Warren is large with no station, and the nearest station depends entirely on where in the township you are (~62-80 min range). Not a point estimate. The Lakeland 78 express from the Warren P&R is the reliable option at 48 min.
Direct NEC to Penn. No PABT bus — Suburban Transit serves Princeton/the Brunswicks, not Edison. Metropark (also Woodbridge, nearby) is the faster express option at ~40 min.
No station, no in-town PABT bus. RVL via Dunellen with a Newark Penn transfer.
Direct NEC, 45 min, walkable downtown station. Rail only — no PABT bus.

One-seat AM-peak to NY Penn. Range is wide and depends entirely on express vs local: express 39-42 min, all-stops local 61 min. Reported 45 = typical peak. NOTE Woodbridge is NOT on the Northeast Corridor timetable (NEC trains bypass it) - North Jersey Coast Line only. Bus 116 a consistent 59 min, runs all day.

Gillette station, M&E Gladstone Branch; typically transfer at Summit. Time taken from the Long Hill row's own note, which recorded all three stations separately (Stirling 68, Gillette 65, Millington 70) — this is that number, not a township average. Bus: Lakeland 78 to PABT, and note it is rush-only with very few trips.

Stirling station, M&E Gladstone Branch; typically transfer at Summit. Time taken from the Long Hill row's own note, which recorded all three stations separately (Stirling 68, Gillette 65, Millington 70) — this is that number, not a township average. Bus: Lakeland 78 to PABT, and note it is rush-only with very few trips.
Midtown Direct one-seat to Penn in 40 min. Train beats the bus comfortably.
36 min one-seat — the FASTEST rail commute in the entire target set. Two stations in town.

Millington station, M&E Gladstone Branch; typically transfer at Summit. Time taken from the Long Hill row's own note, which recorded all three stations separately (Stirling 68, Gillette 65, Millington 70) — this is that number, not a township average. Bus: Lakeland 78 to PABT, and note it is rush-only with very few trips.

No station; Short Hills / Millburn / South Orange are all ~5 mi. Short Hills Midtown Direct ~40 min, excludes drive/park. Community Coach 77 from Livingston Mall Park & Ride to PABT verified 62-73 min, typical 65 (arrives PABT gates 412/413). This is one of the few Essex towns that kept a PABT bus after DeCamp died.
75 min by rail with a forced Newark transfer. The 114 bus is a 2-HOUR local — technically direct, practically unusable. This is a long commute either way.

A section of BRIDGEWATER TWP; inherits the township's Bridgewater station row. NOT an independent measurement — Martinsville sits in the township's north-east and the real drive to Bridgewater or Somerville station will differ. Treat as indicative.

towns.nearest_station_if_none: Orange (in City of Orange Twp, ~1.9 mi)
towns.bus_route: NJT 101 (rush only, ~5 AM trips) + Community Coach 77
towns.notes: No station in town (Highland Ave station is in Orange, not West Orange), but the township runs a weekday jitney to Brick Church/Orange/South Orange, and Orange is a 30-min Midtown Direct ride. Add jitney time. Its DeCamp buses are GONE — NJT 101 replaced them, rush-only.
In Bernards Twp. Gladstone Branch — one of the two AM one-seat trains (6406) actually ORIGINATES here at 6:13, but the typical train requires a Summit transfer.

35-min one-seat to Penn — the 2nd-fastest rail commute in the set, and it's 14 mi from Westfield. LOST its bus: DeCamp 33 served it until 2023 and NJT's replacement routes do NOT stop in town. Rail-only now.

No station. Mountain Ave, Upper Montclair (~1.7 mi) Midtown Direct verified 47-55 min. NO PABT bus: DeCamp 33/66 ran Bloomfield Ave through Verona and is DEFUNCT. The 2023 'emergency' NJT 195D Bloomfield Ave variant is ABSENT from the current 191/195 timetable (issued 7/1/26) - nearest PABT-bound stops are the 195's Cedar Grove stops, ~1 mi outside Verona.

towns.rail_line: M&E Morristown Line (via Madison / Convent Station)
towns.notes: No station, and the nearest is FAR — Madison and Convent Station are both ~5.0 mi, so the 55-min figure (Madison's own one-seat Midtown Direct) excludes a 5-mile drive and park. Same shape as Florham Park, its Hanover Park Regional partner, but at double the distance. No PABT bus: NJT 29/70/71/73/79/871/873/874 all serve the area and every one is a LOCAL Morris/Newark route — verified against the NJT bus GTFS out to 3.5 mi. Private carriers on the Route 10 corridor (Lakeland) were NOT checked, so read this as 'no NJT bus', not 'no bus'. Confidence medium for that reason and the drive.

No station and none close - nearest are the Montclair stops ~4 mi out. Mountain Ave Midtown Direct 47-55 min, excludes a real 4-mi drive. NO PABT bus: DeCamp 33 was the carrier and is defunct; nothing replaced it. Only NJT bus touching Essex Fells is local Route 71, Newark-bound. Transit-poor - this is a car town.

No station. Madison (~2.5 mi) one-seat Midtown Direct verified 51-57 min; Convent Station ~55-61. Excludes drive/park. No PABT bus: NJT 873/878 serve Florham Park but are LOCAL Morris County routes, not PABT.

towns.station_name: Bay Street; Walnut St; Watchung Ave; Upper Montclair; Mountain Ave; Montclair Heights
towns.notes: SIX stations. Bay St is ~43 min one-seat; Montclair Heights ~58. Note the electrified Montclair segment gets Midtown Direct — the diesel Boonton branch beyond it does NOT.

No station; South Orange ~6 mi, one-seat Midtown Direct verified 31-41 min, excludes drive/park (a real 6-mi drive to the station). NO PABT bus - DeCamp was the carrier and is defunct; nothing replaced it. NJT 71/73 serve Roseland but terminate in NEWARK.
No station. DeCamp used to be the commute here and it's gone; NJT 105 replaced it, rush-only. Rail requires driving to Montclair first (45 min excludes that drive).

towns.nearest_station_if_none: Montclair State University (in Little Falls, ~1 mi)
towns.notes: Its station is GONE — Great Notch closed in 2010 (9 riders/day). BUS IS THE BETTER OPTION here: NJT 105 at 45 min beats the 58-min rail workaround via MSU.

No station. Little Falls (~2.5 mi) does NOT run Midtown Direct - NY times are flagged 'change at Newark Broad Street'; verified 58-67 min incl. transfer. Montclair Heights (~2.7 mi) is the better bet: direct Midtown Direct ~52 min. NO PABT bus - DeCamp served North Caldwell and is defunct; no Caldwell-area stops on the current 191/195 timetable.

Third town in 07006. No station of its own; same Bay Street / Walnut Street (Montclair) situation as Caldwell, whose row this is inherited from — same zip, one centroid, one distance. NOT an independent measurement, and the drive/park to Montclair is excluded.
NO station — 'Far Hills-Bedminster' is a marketing name; the station is in Far Hills Borough. It does get a Midtown Direct one-seat, but it's an 85-min ride. No PABT bus.
Clean 50-min Midtown Direct one-seat. No PABT bus in town (nearest is the Summit P&R for Lakeland 78).
55-min Midtown Direct one-seat. Rail only.

No station (the old Erie Greenwood Lake stop is long closed). Bloomfield (~2 mi) Midtown Direct verified 29-35 min. Bus 199 from Kingsland St at Passaic Ave to PABT a consistent 40 min - BUT that stop is on the far-EAST edge of Nutley, not walkable from the Franklin Ave downtown. DeCamp, which served Nutley, is defunct; the 199 is what remains.

towns.bus_route: Trans-Bridge (Municipal P&R, US-202 N) — only 2 AM trips
towns.notes: Technically has a station (North Branch) but it is minimal: single low platform, rush-hour only, ~2 usable AM trains, and RVL forces a Newark transfer anyway. 85 min. Somerville/Raritan are the practical park-and-rides.
62-min Midtown Direct one-seat. LOST its bus — Community Coach 77 was cut back to Livingston Mall and no longer reaches Morristown. Rail only now.

MORRIS TWP wraps around MORRISTOWN and shares its 07960 zip and its Morristown station — zips.json verified them as two distinct MUN_NAMEs on the live Cadastral layer. Inherited from Morristown because it is the SAME STATION, not an independent measurement.

One-seat Midtown Direct on the Gladstone Branch, verified 78-83 min (median 80) — but only 2 AM-peak direct trips (06:10, 06:49). Miss those and it is a change at Summit for ~81 min total. A one-seat ride that exists twice is not a one-seat commute. No NJT bus within 3.0 mi reaches PABT — none at all, in fact. Computed 2026-07-17 from the NJT rail GTFS (weekday 2026-09-04).

Hanover Twp section; no station. Morris Plains (~1.5 mi) one-seat Midtown Direct verified 64-70 min; from Morristown station (~2 mi) the same trains are 59-65. Excludes drive/park. No PABT bus - Lakeland's Route 46 stop list has no Cedar Knolls/Hanover/Whippany/Route 10 stop; NJT 73/871/873/874 are local Newark/Morristown routes.
67-min Midtown Direct one-seat. No PABT bus in town.

One-seat Midtown Direct verified 71-84 min - a long ride. Lakeland 46 from Denville Savage Road Park-Ride (free parking) to PABT ~65 min at peak. Confidence medium: the rail figure is off the current 3/15/26 timetable, but the Lakeland bus minutes come from an ARCHIVED official PDF, not a 2026 timetable (the live page renders via JS) - re-verify the bus before trusting it.

towns.station_name: Glen Rock-Boro Hall; Glen Rock-Main Line
towns.notes: TWO stations, both Hoboken-bound — no Midtown Direct. But the timetabled Secaucus transfer is tight and the effective 50 min is competitive. The 164 bus at 45 min is actually the faster option.
No station and no bus. 62 min is the Morristown ride and EXCLUDES the ~15-min drive to get there. Realistically ~80 min door-to-door.

NO one-seat ride despite having a station — all 5 AM inbound trains terminate at Hoboken, flagged 'change at Newark Broad St'. The diesel Boonton branch never gets Midtown Direct. BUS IS MUCH BETTER: Lakeland 46 at 55 min vs 80 by rail.

Towaco station is in Montville Twp. No one-seat ride (transfer at Newark Broad St). BUS IS FAR BETTER: Lakeland 46 from Pine Brook is 45 min vs 75 by rail — the single biggest bus-beats-train gap in the set.

Has a station and STILL no one-seat ride — same trap as Boonton: the diesel Boonton branch never gets Midtown Direct, so every AM inbound runs to Hoboken and you change at Newark Broad St. Best AM-peak total 84 min. Sanity check: Boonton is one stop closer to NY on the same branch and sits at 80, so 84 is the right side of it. Boonton's saving grace is Lakeland 46 at 55 min; NO NJT bus within 3.0 mi of Mountain Lakes reaches PABT, and private carriers were not checked — treat 'no bus' as 'no NJT bus'. Computed 2026-07-17 from the NJT rail GTFS (weekday 2026-09-04).

towns.bus_route: Coach USA / Rockland-Short Line (Parsons Pond Rd P&R)
towns.notes: No station — the town's own transportation page lists only out-of-town rail. Bergen County Line means a Secaucus transfer. 62 min excludes the drive to Allendale.
Towaco is a SECTION of Montville Twp and is listed separately in zips.json — same station, but no PABT bus stop in Towaco proper (the Lakeland 46 stop is at Pine Brook, elsewhere in Montville).
No station, no in-town bus. Dover gets a Midtown Direct one-seat but it's a 78-min ride and excludes the drive. Nearest bus is Lakeland 46/80 at Dover Terminal.

No station in Chester Boro or Chester Twp. Peapack (~7 mi, distance approximate) has LIMITED one-seat Midtown Direct: 5:59->7:28 (89 min), 6:37->8:12 (95). Most other Gladstone peak trains go to Hoboken or change at Summit. Drivers may prefer Morristown (~10 mi), which has frequent Midtown Direct. No PABT bus on any Lakeland or Community Coach route. LOW confidence: the nearest-station distance is unverified. Effectively a car town.

towns.nearest_station_if_none: Mount Olive (in Mount Olive Twp, ~7 mi)
towns.notes: No station. Mount Olive (~7 mi, approximate) peak trains are DIESEL and run to HOBOKEN, not NY Penn - a change at Dover is required. Worked example incl. a 16-min Dover wait: Mount Olive 6:56 -> Dover 7:17, then Midtown Direct 7:33 -> NY Penn 8:55 = 119 min total. From Hackettstown ~130 min. No PABT bus anywhere in western Morris. The worst commute on this list by a wide margin.
